title: Panorama routing fabric for latency & capacity-aware steering
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a unified multi-region routing fabric ("Panorama") that combines latency-based scoring, geo-pinning heuristics, and capacity-aware steering. Goal: keep p95 latency and availability SLOs across regions while minimizing cross-region traffic and expensive fallbacks. Provide deterministic fallback behavior (circuit breakers + tiered shedding) and observability hooks so Console can show per-route decisions and explainability for routing outcomes.
background: We currently use simple proximity + health checks; during cross-region spikes we see unpredictable failovers that blow past p95 SLOs and increase egress costs.
Existing heuristics don't account for region-level capacity saturation (GPU queue backlog) which leads to cascading latency amplification.
Customer incidents in Q4 2025 showed a pattern: regional throughput saturation -> hedging to distant region -> high latency p95 violations and token cost blowouts.
This initiative ties into runtime-2.4 and Console's exposure of per-request routing decisions so customers can understand cost/latency tradeoffs.
decisions: Routing score = weighted combination of (region_p95_latency, region_capacity_headroom, local_affinity_bonus). Default weights: latency 0.6, capacity 0.3, affinity 0.1.
Geo-pinning: user sessions will be pinned when affinity bonus pushes a region score >= pin_threshold (default 0.8) for the initial 30 minutes of activity.
Circuit breaker thresholds will be configured per-region: open when error_rate > 2% OR p95 increased by >3x baseline for 5m window, half-open probe window 30s.

Load shedding levels: soft shed at queue_depth >= 75% of provisioned concurrency (reject non-critical lower-tier requests), hard shed at >= 95% (reject new requests with 503 and structured explainability).
Fallback chain: local region -> pinned backup (same continent) -> global hedged region. Hedging limited by budget tokens per API key to control cost.
We will expose routing explainability via response headers and Console trace links for sampled requests (consent and privacy-safe).
tradeoffs: More aggressive geo-pinning reduces cross-region egress but can cause localized SLO violations if pinned region saturates.
Weighting capacity higher reduces sudden failovers but may increase average latency for requests that could have been served faster elsewhere.
Shedding non-critical requests protects SLOs but may surface degraded behavior to customers who rely on bulk or background batch features.
Adding detailed explainability increases tracing volume and storage costs; we will sample and cap retention to manage cost.
design_notes: Scoring function implemented as stateless micro-eval: receives region metrics snapshot and request metadata; returns normalized score (0-1).
Region metrics: p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, queue_depth, provisioned_capacity_ratio. Metrics window: 30s sliding for latency, 1m for utilization.
Affinity: token-based session affinity stored in global Redis with TTL; fallback when affinity lookup fails will re-evaluate full scoring.
Circuit breakers live in the front-tier request director to avoid dispatching traffic to unhealthy region pools.
Load shedding integrated with per-tenant priority labels; default priority mapping: realtime=high, interactive=medium, batch=low.
We will maintain a per-region budget controller to enforce egress/cost caps for hedging (configurable per-account).
acceptance_criteria: Routing fabric can route a synthetic traffic mix across 3 regions without causing p95 SLO violations > 10% above baseline under 70% traffic increase.
Circuit breaker opens and recovers according to configured thresholds in test harness; alerts fire to SRE playbook channel.
Load shedding levels trigger at configured queue depths and protect p95 latency for high-priority requests during stress tests.
Console shows per-route routing trace with reason codes for at least 95% of sampled requests; retention policy in place.
End-to-end integration tests and chaos experiments (region outage, degraded NIC) executed and documented in Confluence.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in staging with synthetic region metrics and small traffic mix (2 weeks).
2) Canary: route 1% of production traffic with feature flag + observability enabled; monitor SLOs and cost (1 day).
3) Gradual increase to 10% over 48 hours if no regressions, otherwise rollback and postmortem.
4) Region-by-region enablement: enable for EU first, then NA, then APAC with 72h observation windows.
5) Full rollout behind runtime-2.4 release with canary retention and capacity budget enforcement.
Fallback manual kill-switch available in Console to revert to legacy proximity routing immediately.
monitoring_and_metrics: Per-region: p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate, queue_depth, GPU_util, outstanding_requests
Routing decisions: percent routed to local vs hedged vs pinned; average score components (latency_score, capacity_score, affinity_bonus)
Cost metrics: tokens routed cross-region, hedging token spend by account
SRE alerts: p95 > baseline*1.3 for >5m, regional circuit-breaker opens, shedding rate > 5% of incoming traffic
Dashboards: Panorama routing overview, per-account egress exposure by region, routing explainability sample panel

test_plan: Functional: unit tests for scoring, affinity TTL, and circuit-breaker state transitions.
Integration: staging front-tier + routing fabric with mocked region metrics (p95/queue) and request generator.
Chaos: region kill, NIC flaps, sudden capacity drops; verify hedging limits, shedding behavior, and SLO protection.
Performance: ensure scoring micro-eval latency < 1ms median and < 5ms p99 under load.
Security: data flow audit for affinity metadata to ensure no PII in routing headers.
risk_analysis: Risk: under-allocated hedging budget may cause unexpected throttles for high-value customers. Mitigation: per-account budgets and account-level overrides.
Risk: affinity state store outage could cause loss of pinning leading to jitter in latency. Mitigation: fallback to best-score routing and degrade pin TTL gracefully.
Risk: mis-tuned scores could bias traffic to cheaper but overloaded regions. Mitigation: daily automated calibration job and manual guardrails.
Risk: increased tracing volume from explainability headers. Mitigation: sample fraction and retention caps.
owner_notes: We opted for a principled scoring approach instead of rule tables to make it easier to tune tradeoffs globally and expose weights to advanced customers.
Next milestones: complete front-tier PR, add affinity lookup fallback, and run canary with EU traffic slice.
Keep an eye on hedging token spend during early canaries; SLO protection may look good but cost could spike unexpectedly.
